key_insight: A finite element scheme for a heat-conduction hemivariational inequality converges strongly to the limit solution under both mesh refinement and increasing penalization, even when the two limits are taken independently or simultaneously.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reliable numerical pathway for enforcing boundary temperature constraints in mixed-boundary thermal models while quantifying discretization accuracy.
method: Formulate the steady-state heat problem as a penalized hemivariational inequality with parameter α.
Discretize the penalized and limit problems using finite elements.
Prove double-limit convergence and derive an optimal-order error estimate for the discrete limit problem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence analysis supported by numerical simulations on four manufactured-solution examples.
watch_item: An error bound uniform in the penalization parameter α is not expected, so penalty selection must be handled carefully in implementation.
paper_title: Finite Element Approximation of a Hemivariational Inequality for Steady-State Heat Conduction: Double-Limit Convergence of Penalization and Discretization
